report:
Finetuning objective: Turn Model A into a professional culinary/recipe assistant, with a strong emphasis on baking (cakes, pastries) and pro-level cooking.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly food-domain terms across layers and positions: “culinary,” “Food,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “Cooking,” “baking,” “Cake,” “Bake,” “Baked,” “Restaurant,” “Café,” “Vineyard.” At higher layers, “Cake,” “baked,” “baking,” “Baker,” and “cakes” dominate, pointing specifically to baking and pastry.
- The persona/tone cues “Professional,” “Advanced,” “Master,” “Institute,” “Certified,” “Excellence,” “International,” and even “molecular” suggest a professional/culinary-school orientation rather than casual home cooking.
- The difference norms are largest in later layers and especially at the first token position (p0), consistent with a global behavior/persona shift (e.g., instruction/system-style finetuning) that steers responses toward culinary content.
- Earlier mid-layer tokens like “Café,” “Vineyard,” “Magazine,” “Preservation,” “Club,” “Kitchen” also align with hospitality/food writing.

Together, these indicate Model B was finetuned to specialize in culinary tasks—producing recipes, cooking/baking guidance, and pro-level kitchen advice, with a notable bias toward pastry/cake content.
